_about.chapter: Dialogue and text: the apartment's bonding talks and the bond tiers, the talks (sitting down with Anavia, Mirabel, Ren, the bartender and Dr. Yin), everything the crew says on a night out and in their texts, and the prologue's poem.
_about.how_to_edit: Plain JSON, inlined by tools/build.mjs as GAME_DB.dialogue and checked by tools/test-game-db.cjs. A line is [speaker, text] or { speaker, text, mood }; the speaker is a cast id (949, 747, victoria…) in crew.solo and crew.moments, a name (Victoria, 949) in bonding. {mark}, {gun} and {job} are filled in by the code. Crew members are keyed by name ('747', Victoria, Sabrina, Yenna, Max, Josh). _about.notes keeps the explanations that were comments in the code, keyed by path.

tables.bonding: The apartment's talks (story/dialogue-bonding.js): dialogues (BONDING_DIALOGUES) holds per person, per tier (0 Acquaintance to 3 Inner Circle), a pool of exchanges, one picked each time; tiers (BONDING_TIERS) is each tier's name, the relationship it starts at (min, out of 100), the banner shown on reaching it (message) and the colour of its ring on the contacts app.
tables.crew: The crew's nights out (story/crew-nights.js). A group night: openers (each one's first line), booth (lines at the table), toasts and toast_taste (which toast each one likes) with toast_lines, job_talk (what each says about her last job: bounty, delivery, salvage or none), closers. A solo night: solo (per person: open, ask, opts, the option they like best (liked), replies to each, close), moments (per person, per tier: lines, opts, the good one, and after). Texts: group_invite, yes, no, stood_up, ask_back, intel, stim, solo_ask.
tables.prologue_epigraph: The prologue's poem (PROLOGUE_EPIGRAPH, story/scenes/prologue.js), one line each; an empty string is a stanza break.
tables.talks: The talks (TALKS, story/talks.js): per person, hello, enough (when two new topics are used up today), bye, small (small talk, by tier), topics, and needs (when they can talk at all). A topic is { id, label, tier, needs, key, gain, text, beats }. A beat is [speaker, text, mood] (speaker @ is the person she is talking to), a choice { choose: [options], gain: [rapport each], then: [the beats after each], mem, vals } that remembers what she picked (T.mem[mem] = vals[i]), or { act } that makes something happen. Anything that is code (a line that depends on what she said before, a topic's needs, a gift) is { "hook": "<name>" }: the function TALK_HOOKS[name] in story/talks.js takes its place when the game loads. Topic ids are in save files (questState.talks): never rename one.
tables.talk_ids: The people with talks and their cast ids (TALK_IDS, story/talks.js).

notes.bonding.tiers[0]: `ring` drives the contacts-app avatar border. Kept here so tier colour has one definition — anything else showing tier state reads it from the same place rather than hardcoding a parallel palette.

0.speaker: Victoria
0.text: You just gonna stand there or did you actually want something?
Just checking in.

0.speaker: Victoria
0.text: Checking in. Cute. Well, I'm still here. Still armed. Still better than whoever's out there trying to kill us.
Good to know.

0.speaker: Victoria
0.text: ...Yeah. It is.

0.speaker: Victoria
0.text: This apartment's alright. Small though. You ever think about getting a place with more room to store ammunition?
Not really a priority.

0.speaker: Victoria
0.text: It should be. I've got crates stacked in the corner over there. Organization is half the battle, Freelancer.

1.speaker: Victoria
1.text: You know, I had a corner office once. Real glass. Real view. The kind of place people kill for.
What happened?

1.speaker: Victoria
1.text: I found out what they were actually doing with the weapons I was testing. So I took the prototype and walked out.
Just like that?

1.speaker: Victoria
1.text: Just like that. The glass was bulletproof, by the way. I checked on my way out.

1.speaker: Victoria
1.text: Most people I've worked with are dead or corporate. Same thing, really.
Which am I?

1.speaker: Victoria
1.text: Neither. That's why I'm still here.

2.speaker: Victoria
2.text: I don't say this often and I'll deny it if you repeat it. But this crew? This is the closest thing to family I've had in years.
You don't have to deny it.

2.speaker: Victoria
2.text: ...Fine. But if Max makes one more joke about my hair, I'm putting him through the wall. Lovingly.

3.speaker: Victoria
3.text: Freelancer. Whatever happens out there — whatever comes through those dimensions — I've got you. No hesitation. No questions.

3.speaker: Victoria
3.text: Good. Now let's go break something.

0.speaker: Yenna
0.text: The wind pattern shifts three degrees between 2 AM and 4 AM from that balcony. Affects trajectory past 600 meters.
You've been measuring wind from the apartment?

0.speaker: Yenna
0.text: Observing. There's a difference.

0.speaker: Yenna
0.text: You move well. Not military-trained, but there's something else. Instinct, maybe.
I don't know where it comes from.

0.speaker: Yenna
0.text: That's what makes it dangerous. And useful.

1.speaker: Yenna
1.text: I served three tours in the Rim Conflicts. Saw things that don't make tactical sense. Things that shouldn't exist.
Dimensional anomalies?

1.speaker: Yenna
1.text: That's the polite term. We called them rips. My unit walked into one. I walked out alone.
Yenna...

1.speaker: Yenna
1.text: I don't need sympathy. I need purpose. This crew gives me that.

2.speaker: Yenna
2.text: I've been watching the team dynamics. Victoria leads with force. Sabrina deflects with humor. Max combusts. Josh calculates.

2.speaker: Yenna
2.text: You hold it together. That's the hardest job. And you don't even notice you're doing it.

3.speaker: Yenna
3.text: I don't form attachments easily. But I want you to know — my scope covers you first. Always.

3.speaker: Yenna
3.text: It's not sentiment. It's strategy. You're the one worth keeping alive.

0.speaker: Sabrina
0.text: Oh look, the Freelancer wants to chat. Should I put on tea? Light some candles? Summon a minor demon for ambiance?
Just tea is fine.

0.speaker: Sabrina
0.text: Boring. But sure.

0.speaker: Sabrina
0.text: You know what I like about this apartment? The walls don't bleed. Low bar, but I've lived in worse.
Where was that?

0.speaker: Sabrina
0.text: Nice try. We're not there yet.

1.speaker: Sabrina
1.text: The dark energy thing isn't learned. I was born with it. Mom called it a gift. Dad called it a curse. They were both right.
How do you control it?

1.speaker: Sabrina
1.text: Control is a strong word. I aim it. Big difference.
That's terrifying.

1.speaker: Sabrina
1.text: I know, right? Kind of awesome though.

2.speaker: Sabrina
2.text: I use sarcasm like armor. You've probably noticed.

2.speaker: Sabrina
2.text: It's easier than admitting that I actually care what happens to these idiots. And to you.

2.speaker: Sabrina
2.text: Don't get used to it. But... yeah. It is.

3.speaker: Sabrina
3.text: You're the first person who didn't flinch when they saw what I can do. Not once.

3.speaker: Sabrina
3.text: Because it scares me sometimes. And I'm the one doing it. So thanks for that. Seriously.

0.speaker: Max
0.text: Yo! Finally some company. I was about to start talking to the walls. Again.
Again?

0.speaker: Max
0.text: They don't talk back. It's actually kind of peaceful. Don't judge me.

0.speaker: Max
0.text: Hey, check this out — *bzzt*
Did you just shock the toaster?

0.speaker: Max
0.text: It was being slow. I helped. That's what I do. I help.

1.speaker: Max
1.text: The sparks aren't just some cool party trick. My nervous system is overclocked. Always has been. Too much electricity, not enough... ground.
Is that why you're always moving?

1.speaker: Max
1.text: If I stop, I feel like I'll explode. Not metaphorically. I mean actually explode.
That sounds exhausting.

1.speaker: Max
1.text: It is. But it also means I'll never let you down in a fight. Can't slow down even if I wanted to.

2.speaker: Max
2.text: People think I'm crazy. And like, fair. But there's a reason I burn hot.

2.speaker: Max
2.text: Because the people I care about are worth burning for. This team. You. I'd fry every circuit in my body if it meant keeping you safe.

2.speaker: Max
2.text: Don't make it weird. I'm still gonna shock your toaster.

3.speaker: Max
3.text: You ever notice I don't spark around you anymore? My hands are steady.

3.speaker: Max
3.text: First time that's happened. Ever. You're like a ground wire for me, Freelancer. Don't know what I'd do without this crew.

0.speaker: Josh
0.text: The apartment's network security is inadequate. I've already patched three vulnerabilities.
Thanks, Josh.

0.speaker: Josh
0.text: Acknowledgment noted.

0.speaker: Josh
0.text: You've approached me voluntarily. This is the first time. I'm logging it.
You don't have to log everything.

0.speaker: Josh
0.text: Incorrect. Patterns in social interaction predict mission outcomes with 73% accuracy.

1.speaker: Josh
1.text: I started hacking at age eleven. Not because I wanted to break things. Because I wanted to understand how they worked.
And now?

1.speaker: Josh
1.text: Now I understand how most things work. People are the exception. You are a significant exception.
Is that good or bad?

1.speaker: Josh
1.text: Undetermined. But I find the uncertainty... acceptable.

2.speaker: Josh
2.text: I ran probability models on crew survival rates. With you leading, they're 340% higher than baseline.

2.speaker: Josh
2.text: No. I factored out tactical variables. The remaining variable is morale. You make people want to survive. That's not math. That's... something else.

3.speaker: Josh
3.text: Emotional attachment detected. Subject: you. And the team. Severity: significant. Recommended action: none. I don't want it to stop.
Josh, that might be the most human thing you've ever said.

enough: That's enough of my secrets for one night. Come back tomorrow.
bye: Don't be a stranger.
Go on. Make some noise.
Be careful out there. I mean it.
Come back to me in one piece.
small: The night's slow. Tell me one thing that went right today.
Nobody shot me in the face.
Mm. Mine is faces. Yours is more interesting tonight.
Moon City changed DJs. Worse taste, better volume.
You can hear it from here?
I can hear everything from here. It's why I stand here.
Your crew walked past earlier. The tall one waved. Victoria?
She didn't wave at the man next to me.
I bought a coat today and thought, 949 would laugh at this.
Sit with me a minute. Don't say anything.
I counted. You've come to see me more than anyone else in this city.

topics.label: Ask who she really is
beats: Who am I. You walked all the way over here to ask a woman standing outside a department store who she is.
smile
You're not shopping.
No. Inside, everyone wants something from me. Out here, the wind doesn't know my name.

choose: And what do you want from me?
The wind and I have that in common.
then: Straight to it. Good.
I want to know if you're as good as the noise you make. So far you're louder than you are good.
Oh. She flirts.
sultry
Careful, 949. I collect things I like.
sultry
Don't. People who stop asking stop being interesting.
Ask me again some other night. I might answer.

beats: You know my name. That's more than most people get.

topics.label: Ask about the pistol with her name
beats: That pistol on your hip. Periwinkle bolts. A crackle on the trail.
You're carrying my name around this city, 949. Did you know that?

choose: I thought it was a model number.
It's never jammed on me once.
then: A model number.
smile
My mother would have hated that. Then she'd have sold you a second one.
It wouldn't dare. She built them not to.
The Anavia line was my mother's.
No. Keep it.
sad
It looks right in your hand. Better than it ever looked in mine.
The line was my mother's. She named it after me the year I was born.

beats: Someday I'll tell you the rest. Not on a sidewalk.
topics.text: Clean that pistol tonight. She'd want it shining.

topics.label: Ask why she stands outside Enni Cole
beats: Every night, the same spot. Why here?
Valentina won't let me past the doors since last season.

choose: Want me to talk to her?
then: I bought the entire spring couture rack. Then I returned it. Wearing all of it.
grin
Valentina called it theatre. I called it a review.
You? Walk in there and plead my case?
smile
Sweet. No. I like being the most interesting thing on this street.
Mm. Everything is, eventually.
sultry

beats: Besides. From here I can see Moon City's door. You'd be surprised who comes and goes.

topics.label: Ask why she pays so well for scrap
beats: You pay well for scrap. Nobody pays well for scrap.
Everything this city throws away, someone paid for once. I'm collecting what they forgot.

choose: As long as the pay clears.
then: No. It's a door.
You'll find the handle if you keep coming back.
sultry
A collection. Some of it belonged to people I loved.
Bring me the crates. Don't open them.
It clears. It always clears with me.
I hoped you'd be curious. Pity.

topics.label: Ask about her mother
beats: The Anavia house. Pistols like art. Every one tuned by hand, every bolt the colour of the evening I was born.
Then the debts came. A company bought the house, the designs, the name. Everything but me.
Which company?
W. MINDUSTRIAL.
Your Mirabel.

then: Isn't she? She calls, you come.
Don't look at me like that. I'm not asking you to choose. Yet.
Of course you do. Everyone does. She pays like a storm.
Just remember who's standing under it.
She bought the house for the patents and shut the workshop within a week. Mother didn't last the year.
sad
I don't hate her. Hate is a luxury. I just don't forget.

beats: That's the most I've said about it to anyone. Don't make me regret it.
topics.text: Thank you for listening tonight. I don't say that.

topics.label: Ask what's really in the crates
beats: The crates I clear for you. They're not random freight.
…No.
When the house was sold, Mother hid her last designs. Shipped in pieces, under false manifests, all over the city.
Every crate you bring me is one more piece of her.

choose: What's my cut of a dead woman's legacy?
then: Because people treat things differently when they know they matter.
You'd have slowed down. Gotten careful. Gotten killed.
Don't promise. Promises are how she lost everything.
sad
…But thank you.
smile
Same as always. Scrap and personics.
annoyed
Ask me that again and you can go dig up someone else's mother.
angry

topics.label: Listen to the music with her
beats: Listen. Moon City's bass carries all the way here at this hour.
Do you dance, 949?

choose: Only when someone's shooting at me.
then: That's not dancing. That's survival with rhythm.
grin
Though I've seen you work. It's close.
Good. People who dance well never look at you.
smile
Hm.
sultry
Stella. Would you give me one dance, some night when nobody's paying either of us?
Then I'll hold you to it.
smile
Maybe is a door too.
sultry

topics.label: Ask what scares her
beats: You want to know what I'm afraid of.
I didn't ask.
You were about to. You have the face for it.
Being wanted for what I have. The money, the caches, the name. Never for the woman standing here in the cold.
sad

choose: I came back for the woman.
Everyone wants something. I want you to be okay.
then: …You did. Every time. I counted.
smile
Bold. Honest. A terrible combination.
smile
Ha. Both. Fine. Both.
grin

topics.text: Still cold out here. Less, though.

topics.label: Ask about the last crate
beats: The last piece came in. Your crate.
It wasn't a pistol. It was a pattern. She designed clothes before she ever built a gun.
A periwinkle crop top, a long skirt, gold heels. She made it for me, for a gala that never happened.
I want you to have it.

choose: I'll wear it on a night that matters.
It's yours. Wear it for her.
then: You can. You will. I'm not asking.
smile
Then I'll be there to see it.
smile
I tried. It fits you better. It always did.
sad

topics.text: Send me a picture when you wear it. Don't argue.

topics.label: Stay with her a while
beats: Can I tell you something nobody in this city knows?
Anavia isn't my name. It was the line's. When Mother died I took it, so it would still mean something, walking around.
What's your real name?
Lena.
Nobody has called me that in eleven years.
sad

then: …Again. Slower.
sad
Lena.
There. Now someone in this city knows me.
smile
It does now. Because you say it like it's mine.
smile
I know you will. That's why you got it.
smile

beats: Stay a while, 949. Not for a job. Just stay.

then: Good.
smile
I'll take it. I'll take all of them.
smile
Soon. You keep saying that, and I keep believing you.
sad

enough: I have a board meeting in my head. Tomorrow, 949.
bye: Don't keep me waiting next time.
Go. W. MINDUSTRIAL remembers.
Mind yourself out there.
Come back soon. That is an order, and also a request.
small: The champagne here is dreadful. I keep ordering it.
Because I own the vineyard. It's penance.
My board wants quarterly projections. I want a nap.
Sit. Tell me about your crew. The loud one, Max. Is he as tiresome as he looks?
Worse. He'd take a bullet for any of us.
Hm. Then he's worth the noise.
I cleared an hour on my calendar and labelled it "949." My assistant asked if you were a project.
You're the only one I enjoy.

topics.label: Ask what the Dark Maker took from her
beats: The Dark Maker. What did he do to you?
He took something from me that can't be insured.

choose: So you hired me for revenge.
then: A face. Someone I would have burned this city down for.
sad
Don't ask whose. Not yet.
I know you will. That's why the others aren't sitting in this room.
Revenge is for people without a legal department.
This is housekeeping.

topics.label: Ask what W. MINDUSTRIAL makes
beats: What does your company actually make?
Minds, darling. Not the thinking kind. The kind you install.
Half the augments under this city's skin passed through one of my labs first.

choose: Then I owe you for my reflexes.
Does Dr. Yin buy from you?
then: Everything worth having is.
You owe me for a great deal more than that. We'll settle up some day.
smile
Dr. Yin buys from whoever is best. Today, that's me. Tomorrow I intend it to be me as well.

topics.label: Ask about "starry heavens"
beats: Starry heavens. You say it a lot.
My father was an astronomer. He said it whenever the telescope showed him something he couldn't afford to understand.
Vanoga, mostly. He spent his life looking at one star.

choose: He sounds like a good man.
then: Every night. From the roof of my tower, where nobody can see me do it.
smile
He was a poor one. Those two things are connected, I've found.
Careful. I've had people dismissed for less.
annoyed

topics.label: Ask about Anavia's mother
beats: Anavia told me about her mother's house.
Did she.
Then she told you I bought it. Did she tell you it was already sinking? That I paid three times what anyone else offered?

choose: She said you shut the workshop.
then: I did. The workshop was killing her mother faster than the debt was.
sad
Nobody remembers that part. I don't need them to.
Because that woman made beautiful things, and I wanted them to exist after her.
Sentiment. Don't spread it around.
Wise. Stay that way, and you'll keep both of us.

topics.label: Ask "Why me?" again
beats: In the van you said nobody had ever disappointed you less. Why does that matter so much?
Because everyone disappoints, 949. My father. My board. The man I hired before you.
I built my whole life around expecting it.
You're the only line in my ledger that keeps coming out even.

then: I didn't say perfect. I said even. It's rarer.
I won't. That frightens me more than the Dark Maker does.
smile
Perhaps. Start with yourself, and I'll watch.
smile

beats: Here. A retainer. Don't argue. It's tax-deductible.
topics.text: W. MINDUSTRIAL remembers its friends. So do I.

enough: Rush hour's coming. Tomorrow? I'll save the good beans.
bye: Drive safe!
Don't let Koda see you leave without a pastry.
Text me when you get home, okay?
Love you. Go. I mean, go.
small: Someone ordered a decaf with three extra shots. I think they're confused about life.
Koda burned his hand on the steamer and blamed the steamer. Out loud. For ten minutes.
You look tired. Do you ever sleep?
I named the new blend after you. Don't laugh.
Nine Lives. It's very strong and nobody can kill it.

topics.label: Ask how Amber started
beats: Amber? Koda, me, one scooter, and a lot of cold soup.

choose: You built that from a scooter?
then: One scooter, one map, and a lot of yelling.
grin
Now the app does the yelling.
The scooter was slow. The soup was not a soup by the end.
grin
We put lids on everything after that. Hence the boxes.
You're our best one. The ratings don't lie.
smile
Okay, they lie a little. But not about you.

topics.label: Ask about Chef Koda
beats: Is Koda always that grumpy?
Koda isn't grumpy. Koda is a perfectionist with a bad back.
He took me in when I was fourteen. I stole a croissant from this exact counter.

then: He said a thief who picks the best croissant has a palate. Then he made me wash dishes for a year.
It is. Don't tell him I said that. He'll cry and blame the onions.
smile
The best I've ever had. I've been trying to make one that good for nine years.
grin

topics.label: Ask about the regulars
beats: See the man by the window? Same tea, every day, for six years. He has never drunk it.

choose: Some people need a reason to sit somewhere.
then: Once. He said "not yet" and tipped me double.
…That's actually beautiful. I'm giving him a fresh one tomorrow.
smile
Oh no. Now I'm going to cry into the milk.
sad

topics.label: Ask what she really wants
beats: What do you want, Ren? Not for the café. For you.
A roastery. Up in the hills where the beans grow. Somewhere the city's noise doesn't reach.

then: Probably. I'd bring a radio. And Koda. Same thing.
grin
Deal. You'd have to learn to sleep, though.
smile
You would, wouldn't you. You'd just show up with a truck.
smile
Okay. Don't look at me, I'm fine. It's the steam.
sad

topics.text: Looked at a map of the hills tonight. Just looking.

topics.label: Talk about last week
beats: Can I say something? Last week you came in bleeding, and you smiled at me like nothing happened.
Don't do that. Not with me.
sad

choose: I didn't want to scare you.
then: I know it's the job. I'm not asking you to quit. I'm asking you to let me worry.
You scared me more by pretending.
sad
Okay.
smile
Okay. That's all I wanted.
smile

topics.text: Your mug is clean and waiting. Come home in one piece.

enough: I've got a bar to run. Tomorrow.
bye: Watch the door on your way out.
Drinks are on the house next time.
Stay alive. Bad for business otherwise.
Go on. Your seat stays yours.
small: Some kid tried to pay with a cracked personics chip. I gave him water and a lecture.
The lecture. He drank the water anyway.
Your sniper friend sat at the end of the bar for an hour. Didn't drink. Just watched the door.
Good customer. Never breaks a glass.

topics.label: Ask his name
beats: I don't even know your name.
Bartender's fine. In this business, names get people killed.

then: Sure. Mine's in a drawer somewhere, with my old life.
Smart. You'd be surprised how few people let it go.
Ha. Many have tried.
grin
Go on, then. One guess a visit.

topics.label: Ask where the bounties come from
beats: People leave names on napkins. Under glasses. Folded into tips.
I just read the napkins.

then: People who lost something. People who want something. Same people, mostly, a week apart.
It's a bar in a city like this. Grim is the house special.
For you? I'll start reading the floor too.
grin

topics.label: Ask about the crew's booth
beats: You and your crew. The back booth. You know you're the only table that tips the band?
Victoria, mostly. She tips like she's apologising for something.

then: Most people are. She's just honest about it.
It's yours. I put a reserved sign on it. Nobody reads it, but it's there.
smile
Your hacker counts the exits. Your sniper counts the people. The loud one counts the drinks.
You count them. All of them. Every time.

topics.label: Ask about Mirabel's lounge
beats: I pour for her too. One glass of Vanoga red a night. She never finishes it.

then: My guess? She orders it for someone who isn't here any more.
It's the job. The drinks are the easy part.
I don't tell anybody anything. It's why everyone tells me everything.
grin

enough: I have three patients waiting and one of them is on fire. Tomorrow.
bye: Hydrate.
Come back before something breaks, not after.
Take care of what I built.
Stay whole, 949.
small: Your left shoulder is two degrees higher than your right.
It means you carry something heavy. Pick a side.
I ate lunch today. Sitting down. Write that in the history books.
Don't be. It was cold noodles.
You haven't been back with a wound in a while.

topics.label: Ask what Resonance is
beats: Every augment hums at a frequency. Resonance is how well yours hum together.
Yours hum… loudly.

then: Loud is powerful. Powerful is dangerous. Dangerous is my business.
I could. You'd be slower. I don't think you want slower.
Loud is good until it isn't. I'll tell you when.

topics.label: Ask why she patches up freelancers
beats: Why freelancers? The hospitals pay better.
The hospitals ask for papers. Blood doesn't carry papers.

then: I've practised it.
smile
No.
The rest is that someone patched me up once, with no questions, on a night I couldn't have answered any.
So am I. Don't make me regret it on the table.
smile

topics.label: Ask if an augment ever went wrong
beats: Once. A boy, nineteen. He wanted reflexes faster than his nerves could carry.
I said no. Someone else said yes.
sad

choose: Is that why you check me so often?
then: I know. Knowing doesn't help as much as people think.
sad
He moved faster than anyone I've ever seen. For eleven days.
Yes.
Every time you come in, I count your heartbeats twice.

topics.label: Ask what she sees in your scans
beats: You heal faster than you should, 949.
Your scans don't match anything in my library. Not human baseline. Not any augment I've installed.

then: I don't know yet. That's the honest answer, and I don't like giving it.
It's in no file but my own head. It stays there.
smile
Then I'll know it for you, until you do.

topics.text: Ran your numbers again. Still impossible. Still you. Sleep.

747: There she is. Sit, Nine. Tonight we're off the clock.
Victoria: Nine! Finally. I ordered for you. Don't ask what it is.
Sabrina: Look who remembered she has friends.
Max: You're late. Sit down before someone takes your seat.
Josh: You arrived four minutes after the median. Acceptable.
Yenna: Booth with a clear view of both exits. You're welcome.

booth.747: Good to see everyone in one piece for once.
booth.Victoria: The DJ keeps looking at me. I'm going to let him suffer.
booth.Sabrina: The drinks here are terrible. I've had four.
booth.Max: Music's too loud. Drinks are too small. This is bullshit.
booth.Josh: Fun fact: this booth has the best acoustics in the building. For eavesdropping.
booth.Yenna: Bartender's been watering the gin. I can tell from here.

toast_lines.Yenna: To the crew. Every one of you.

toast_lines.Josh: Technically we get paid either way. But yes.

bounty.Yenna: That last mark had a decent rifle. Had.
bounty.Josh: {job}. Closed. I put a little star next to it.
bounty.Victoria: Can we talk about how dramatic that last bounty was?

delivery.747: Honest work. Nothing wrong with that.
delivery.Victoria: I hear we're couriers now. Do I get a cute hat?
delivery.Josh: Amber rated you five stars. I checked. Twice.
delivery.Max: Boxes. We fought gods and now we carry boxes.
delivery.Sabrina: How's the delivery life? Tips any good?
delivery.Yenna: Delivery routes are good recon. Smart.

salvage.747: Careful with Anavia, Nine. Her gifts have strings.
salvage.Max: Anavia's scrap jobs pay. I'll give her that.
salvage.Josh: That salvage haul was worth more than this bar.
salvage.Victoria: You came back covered in rust. Iconic.
salvage.Yenna: Salvage guards are getting smarter. Watch it.
salvage.Sabrina: Treasure hunting for Anavia. How romantic.

none.747: Enjoy the quiet while it lasts.
none.Victoria: Quiet week. I hate quiet weeks.
none.Max: Nothing's blown up in days. I'm suspicious.
none.Josh: Statistically, something terrible is about to happen.

closers.747: Same time next week. Nobody dies before then.
closers.Victoria: Okay, I'm drunk. Somebody walk me to a car.
closers.Sabrina: Last round. Then I'm going home. Alone. Probably.
closers.Max: Fine. That wasn't terrible. Don't tell anyone I said that.
closers.Josh: I'll put it on the group card. You're welcome.
closers.Yenna: I'll take the back door. Old habits.

open: Nine. I got you the usual. Black, too strong.
Sit. No contracts tonight. Just coffee.
ask: Settle something for me. What's the point of all this, after the jobs?
replies: …Yeah. Me too. Funny how that turns into the whole point.
Hm. Take me with you when you disappear. I'll carry the bags.
Don't let him become the only thing you are, Nine.
close: Same time next week? Coffee's on me.

open: victoria
Okay, look at this. LOOK at it. Torque got the new wraps in.
victoria
I need a second opinion. A good one. Not Max's.
ask: Which one? Be honest. Be very honest.
replies: Classy. Bit safe. I love you anyway.
Matte black is what Max would pick. I'm hurt.
YES. Finally, someone with taste. I'm putting it on your car.
close: This was fun. You're fun. Don't tell the others, they'll get jealous.

open: sabrina
You came. I was starting to think I'd have to drink alone. Again.
sabrina
Sit. The bartender knows my order. He'll guess yours.
ask: Tell me something nobody else in the crew knows about you.
opts: I hate the sound of rain.
replies: Rain. In this city. You poor thing.
Everyone does. You're just honest about it.
Ha. Good. Keep your secrets, Nine. It suits you.

open: yenna
Cans are set up on the rail. Fifty paces.
yenna
Loser buys dinner. I've never bought dinner.
opts: Shoot the can she's aiming at.
replies: …Clean. You actually listened when I taught you.
Missed by a mile. But it looked cool.
Did you just— okay. That's funny. I hate that it's funny.
close: Same spot next time. I'll bring a harder target.

open: josh
Prisma has a sale on V.O.C.A.L.s. I've been here for two hours.
josh
I need you to stop me from buying a voice that sounds like a cello.
opts: The one that sounds like Max.
replies: You're enabling me. I appreciate it. I'm not buying it.
…That's the nicest thing anyone's said to me this month.
This is bullshit. See? It works. Terrifying.
close: Thanks for coming. I logged it as a team-building exercise.

open: max
Don't laugh.
max
I need an opinion on a jacket. One opinion. Yours.
replies: I look like Josh in this. Never mind.
Of course. Of course you say that.
close: This was… fine. Good. It was good. Don't make it weird.

lines: You ever think about the first job? The one in the rain?
You froze for half a second. I almost didn't see it.
opts: You saw. Thanks for not saying anything.
after: That's what partners are for, Nine.

lines: Mirabel asked me how you're holding up.
I told her you're fine. Are you?
opts: Not really. But I will be.
after: That's a better answer. I've got you.

lines: If something happens to me out there, I want you to lead them.
They listen to you more than you think.
opts: Nothing's going to happen to you.
after: You don't get to promise that. But thanks.
Good. Then I can sleep tonight.

lines: I'd follow you anywhere, Nine. Into anything.
after: Too late. It's out there now.

lines: Can I tell you something embarrassing?
I practise my one-liners in the mirror. Before jobs.
after: Right?! Finally someone appreciates the craft.
Wow. Okay. I'm telling everyone you snore.

lines: Max says I talk too much on comms.
after: HA. He does. I'm keeping that one.
Traitor. A cute traitor, but a traitor.

lines: I'm scared all the time out there. I just make it look fabulous.
after: …Okay. Okay, that helps more than you know.
Thanks. I think. That's the whole trick.

lines: You're my favourite. Out of everyone. Don't tell 747.
after: I KNEW it. Okay, I'm crying. Ignore me.
You wouldn't dare. …You would. I love that about you.

lines: You check corners the way I taught you. I noticed.
after: Don't let the others hear that. They'll sulk.

lines: I keep a list. Every shot I didn't take.
It's a short list. It still bothers me.
opts: Those are the ones that count.

lines: I trust you on my blind side. I don't say that to people.
after: I know. That's why I said it.

lines: When this is all over, I'm buying a place with a view of nothing. No rooftops. No angles.
There's a room in it for you.
opts: You'd be bored in a week.

lines: Everyone thinks I'm mean. I'm just accurate.
opts: You're kinder than you let on.

lines: Victoria tried to braid my hair on the last job. Mid-firefight.
after: …She did a good job. I hate it.

lines: I used to work alone. Liked it.
after: Yeah. Turns out I don't mind.

lines: If you ever leave the crew, I'm coming with you. I'm not asking.

after: Engines. Rain on a tin roof. This crew, mostly.

lines: Josh fixed my rifle sight while I was asleep. Didn't say a word.
I don't know what to do with that.
after: …Yeah. Yeah, that's better. I like that.

lines: I lose my temper. On jobs. You know that.
You never hold it against me.
after: I always will. For you lot.
Fair. I'll work on it. Probably.

lines: I had a sister. She'd have liked you.
That's all. I just wanted you to know.
I keep a file on everyone in the crew. For safety.
Yours is the thinnest. That bothers me.
Statistically, we should be dead four times over.
after: That's not how statistics work. But I'll allow it.
I can't. It's how I relax.

lines: Everyone says "you're welcome" is my thing.
It's because nobody ever said thank you first.
I rewrote my file on you. It's one line now.
"Would die for her." Then I deleted it. Too dramatic.

group_invite.text: Drinks. Moon City. First round's on Josh.
Booth at Moon City tonight. Don't make me drink with Max alone.
Calendar invite: Moon City, tonight. Attendance is mandatory. Kind of.

stood_up.Josh: Your seat was empty. I noticed.

ask_back.Max: …Sure. I need help with something anyway.
ask_back.Josh: Yes. I mean, I'm free. Yes.

intel.747: Heads up. {mark}'s carrying a {gun}. Stay behind cover.
intel.Sabrina: Your mark's packing a {gun}. Try not to get shot.
intel.Max: {mark} has a {gun}. Don't do anything stupid.
intel.Josh: Pulled {mark}'s file. They carry a {gun}. You're welcome.

stim.747: Left a stim in your bag. Don't argue.
stim.Victoria: You looked rough. There's a stim in your pocket. You're welcome, darling.
stim.Yenna: Stim in your kit. Use it.
stim.Sabrina: Slipped you a stim. Don't make it a habit.
stim.Max: Stim. Your bag. Don't make me patch you up.
stim.Josh: Restocked one stim. Logged as a gift.

747: Cafe's quiet tonight. Your usual's getting cold.
No contracts. Just coffee. Cozy Cafe, Nine.
Saved us the seat by the fire. Come sit.
Victoria: Torque's open late. Come judge my paint choices.
I need you at the garage. It's urgent. It's about rims.
Sabrina: Bar's quiet tonight. Come be quiet with me.
I'm at Moon City. Drinking alone is a choice and I'm un-choosing it.
Booth at the back. Bring your bad jokes.
Yenna: Range is clear. Fifty paces. Loser buys.
Park, after dark. The cans miss you.
Need a spotter. Not for work.
Josh: Neural Systems got a new shipment. I require supervision.
I've booked thirty minutes for us. That came out wrong. Come to Neural Systems.
Max: Enni Cole. I need a second opinion. Again. Shut up.
Found a jacket. Need your eyes. Don't tell Victoria.
Come to Enni Cole. Don't make it weird.

prologue_epigraph: You come alone? Who do you think you are?
You’re an old collection of screws and wire,
Complete with low grade ditanium plating,
Nothing but a façade of a person,
Where’s your crew? Your parade of bickering kids?
Your group of so-called Freelancers… ha…
You’re nothing but a pawn… a pawn in a game, ages old.
